h1: Feel@Chill Resort — a small clean resort with a pool in Klong Son, near the Koh Chang pier
intro: Picture this: a small resort of around 10 rooms in the village of Klong Son in the north of Koh Chang — spotless modern rooms, a small pool to cool off in, Thai owners who greet you like an old friend, and a quiet setting with no thumping bar music like the party strip — Feel@Chill Resort Koh Chang is a stay for people who want "value and peace of mind" more than luxury · The key thing to understand before you book: it sits along the main road in Klong Son, not on the beach, so reaching the sea means a car or motorbike out to the shore · In return you get a spot just about 5 minutes from the ferry pier, clean rooms, a private pool, and a price that's genuinely within reach · Rooms start at around ฿1,300/night, scored about 8.4 from real guest reviews.

body.html: The big picture and who it suits — If I had to put it in one line, Feel@Chill Resort Koh Chang is a small resort that plays the "value" and "peace of mind" cards rather than selling luxury or sea views like a beachfront property · It's a small place of around 10 rooms in the village of Klong Son in the north of Koh Chang, run hands-on by its Thai owners · Its position is clear: a clean modern stay with a small pool to cool off in, at a price several times lower than the beachfront resorts · From real reviews across several platforms, the people it suits best are couples or travelers who can ride a motorbike and want to use the resort as a base for exploring the island, people who arrive on the island in the evening and want to stay near the pier before moving on, and budget travelers who care more about cleanliness and quiet than walking down to the beach from their room · On the flip side, if you're set on lazing on the sand all day, walking straight from your room to the sea, or traveling with small kids who need full facilities, this may not be the answer — consider a beachfront resort at Klong Prao or Kai Bae instead · To be blunt, Feel@Chill is a "good budget stay" that does its job well within its price bracket; it isn't trying to be a full-scale resort, and that's exactly why one group of guests loves it so much.

Location and getting around — This is the part to get straight, because it directly affects your decision · Feel@Chill Resort sits at 20/1 Moo 3, Ban Khlong Son Road, Klong Son, Koh Chang, a fishing village and local community at the far north of the island's west coast · The location's strength is that it's just about 5 minutes by car from the ferry pier (Ao Sapparot / Centerpoint Ferry), a real advantage for anyone arriving in the evening or needing an early-morning getaway, with no long drive deep into the island · From the hotel it's about 10 minutes by car to White Sand Beach, the main tourist strip, with Klong Prao and Kai Bae a bit further on · Nearby you'll also find waterfalls, elephant-viewing spots, and Mu Ko Chang National Park within about a 15-minute drive · The single most important thing to note is that it's not on the beach — the resort is along the main road, there's no sea view from the rooms, and reaching the water means a car or motorbike · For that reason many real reviews agree you should rent a motorbike, since relying on the island's songthaews costs money and means waiting · If you ride confidently, this Klong Son location becomes an advantage because it's near the island's exit and reaches several beaches; but if you don't drive at all, plan your transport carefully before booking.

"Arrived on the island in the evening and it was just a five-minute drive from the pier to the resort — so convenient. The room was spotless, the owner was kind and chatty, and that night I slept great with total silence and no noise at all. In the morning I had a soak in the little pool before heading out — really worth what I paid."

Rooms and decor — Feel@Chill has around 10 rooms in total, which gives it a friendly feel — more like staying at a friend's place than a big hotel · The rooms are simple and modern, with tiled floors and light-toned walls, understated but neatly done · Inside you get AC, a flat-screen TV with satellite channels, a small fridge, tea/coffee making facilities, a sofa sitting corner, and a private bathroom with hot water, a shower, and a separate toilet and shower area · What real reviews praise most consistently is the cleanliness and beds that are more comfortable than the price suggests — many people say they woke up refreshed because they slept well, and the rooms look new and well kept · Some rooms have a small balcony or a window looking out over the pool and garden, while others face the road · Details like soundproof windows in some rooms also help make for a quieter night · To be honest, these aren't luxe rooms loaded with extras — no bathtub, no sea view, and the space isn't huge — but in terms of "a clean, new, comfortable room at this price," they do it so well it's the main selling point here · If you care about good-quality rest without paying a lot, Feel@Chill's rooms deliver real value.

Facilities and the pool — Even as a small resort, Feel@Chill has the essentials covered for an easygoing stay · The highlight of the common area is the small outdoor pool with sun loungers in the middle of the resort, where guests can soak and cool off after a day out · Be realistic — this is a pool for "cooling off" rather than serious laps, since it isn't large, but it's enough for a 10-room resort and a spot the kids love · Beyond the pool there's a BBQ corner for grilling, free parking for both cars and motorbikes, free Wi-Fi throughout, luggage storage, and a transfer service · Some booking channels list a pier/airport transfer service (possibly for an extra fee), which is handy for anyone who didn't drive themselves · One thing to know: some booking-site listings may mention a spa or fitness center, but from checking reviews and the latest information, this place has no full spa or fitness center — it's a small resort that focuses on the essentials rather than a full set of facilities · If you set your expectations at "a small clean resort with a pool and parking," you won't be disappointed; but if you're hoping for a spa, gym, or lots of on-site activities, that's not what this place was designed for.

Food and the café — Feel@Chill has a small café/restaurant on site serving Thai food, coffee, drinks, and breakfast · The café is a relaxed corner to hang out in, and real reviews mention it warmly as something that adds to the resort's charm — good for sipping coffee in the morning before heading out or relaxing in the evening · Breakfast is served in the morning (some channels list roughly 7:00–10:00 AM) with a simple menu in both Western and Thai styles · To be honest, the food here is the "simple but okay" kind rather than a luxury-resort restaurant, and the menu options aren't extensive · But the upside of the Klong Son location is that it's surrounded by local eateries and fishing-village restaurants with friendly prices and honest flavors, so many people choose to ride out and eat outside the resort to soak up the local community feel · If you want fresh, affordable seafood, Klong Son has the edge because it's a fishing village · Overall, food isn't the reason to come here to eat in the resort; it's a supporting feature done just right, in keeping with a stay that uses the resort as a base for exploring the island.

Service and the owners — One of the most consistently praised things in real reviews is the friendly, attentive Thai owners and staff · Because it's a small resort the owners run themselves, many guests feel warmly welcomed, with someone on hand to recommend places, sort out transfers, arrange motorbike rentals, or book tours · The service feels like "staying at a friend's place" rather than a formal hotel, which many people like because it feels relaxed and unstuffy · The service score in real reviews is fairly high, reflecting that the people are the strong point here · Of course, being a small resort comes with limits — there's no 24-hour front desk like a big hotel, and some services need advance notice — but overall the care for guests is a big reason people come back and recommend it.

What real reviews say (praise and gripes) — Pulling together feedback from Trip.com, Booking.com, Agoda, and Thai-language reviews, the picture is fairly consistent · On the praise side: room cleanliness is mentioned most, comfortable beds, rooms that look new and well kept; friendly, helpful Thai owners and staff; a quiet setting with no bar music like the party strip; a small pool to cool off in; a location near the ferry pier that's convenient for travel; and most importantly the value for money, which many people rank as the number-one strength · On the gripe side: the most-mentioned issue is that it's not on the beach — you need a car or motorbike to reach the sea, which leaves non-drivers feeling it's inconvenient · Next is the small pool, better for soaking than serious swimming; the roadside location with no sea view and unremarkable surroundings; limited common areas and on-site activities; and a small range of food at the resort · Almost all of these gripes come down to setting the right expectations — this place isn't trying to be a full beachfront resort; it's a small, clean, great-value stay that does its job well.

"The room was so clean for the price and the owner was lovely and helped with everything · My only gripe is it's not on the beach — you have to ride a motorbike out to swim — but if you've rented a bike it's no problem. I'll be back next time."

Price comparison and value — Feel@Chill's starting price is around ฿1,300/night at regular rates (there have been deals from around 38 dollars/night), and it can climb during high season or long weekends, but it still sits in Koh Chang's budget bracket · Compared with the island's beachfront resorts that start much higher, the selling point here is clear: you get a clean, new modern room plus the resort's own pool, at a price several times lower than a beachfront resort · Value for money is the highest score across several real-review sources, which matches this place's character exactly · If your plan is to use the resort as a good-quality place to sleep and rest, then head out to the various beaches all day, the money you save on the room can go toward activities, diving, or food · But if you intend to laze on the beach all day without going anywhere, paying more for a beachfront resort may be better value for that style of stay · In short, Feel@Chill is great value for the "explorer who uses the resort as a base" and less so for the "laze-on-the-beach" traveler.

Things to know before booking — A few things help make a stay at Feel@Chill run smoothly · One, get your transport sorted — since it's not on the beach and sits in a local village, rent a motorbike or ask about transfer services in advance; if you don't drive, plan your songthaew situation carefully · Two, set your expectations to match what you get — this is a small, clean, budget resort, not a full beachfront resort; there's no spa/fitness center, and the pool is a small one for soaking · Three, make the most of the location near the pier — it's ideal for the first night when you arrive on the island in the evening, or the last night before an early-morning departure, since it's just about 5 minutes from the pier · Four, check the season — during Koh Chang's rainy season (roughly May–October) the sea and some activities are limited, and some resorts and shops on the island may close, so check before booking and ask the property directly · Five, book ahead and compare platforms — with only around 10 rooms it fills up fast in high season, and choose free cancellation first if your plans aren't certain.

The verdict — From all the real reviews, Feel@Chill Resort Koh Chang is the best fit for people who want a clean, new room with a pool at a budget price, using the resort as a base to explore Koh Chang · The room cleanliness, the warm Thai owners, the quiet setting with no bar noise, and the location near the ferry pier make it a value pick that's hard to beat in the same price bracket · If you're looking for a beachfront stay you can walk to the sea from, want a spa, gym, and full facilities, or aren't comfortable getting around the island, this may not be the answer — consider a beachfront resort at Klong Prao or Kai Bae instead · But for travelers who can ride a motorbike and value good value, cleanliness, and quiet, with a friendly welcome — Feel@Chill answers that need well at a friendly price, and that's why it keeps scoring high on value in real reviews.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Feel@Chill Resort Koh Chang

faq.q: Is Feel@Chill Resort on the beach · how do you get to the beach?
faq.a: Not on the beach · the resort is along the main road in Klong Son village in the north of Koh Chang · to swim in the sea you need to take a car or ride a motorbike out to the beach, such as Klong Son Beach about 5 minutes away or White Sand Beach about 10 minutes · this is something to understand before booking — renting a motorbike of your own is the most convenient option.

faq.q: Where on Koh Chang is Feel@Chill Resort · is it near the pier?
faq.a: It's in Klong Son in the north of Koh Chang's west coast, at 20/1 Moo 3, Ban Khlong Son Road · its strength is that it's just about 5 minutes by car from the ferry pier, ideal for the first night arriving on the island in the evening or the last night before leaving · White Sand Beach is about 10 minutes, and Mu Ko Chang National Park about 15 minutes.

faq.q: What's the starting price at Feel@Chill Resort · what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start at around ฿1,300/night (there have been deals from around 38 dollars) for a Standard room · there are Superior, Deluxe, and Family Rooms for small families, starting from around ฿1,600 up · it's a small resort with only around 10 rooms, fills up fast in high season, so book ahead and compare platforms before booking.

faq.q: What stands out about Feel@Chill Resort?
faq.a: Its strengths are clean, new modern rooms, comfortable beds, a small pool, and a budget price that's excellent value · plus warm, friendly Thai owners, a quiet setting with no bar noise, and a location near the ferry pier · the value-for-money category scores the highest in real reviews.

faq.q: Who is Feel@Chill Resort good for?
faq.a: Good for couples and travelers who can ride a motorbike, who value value, cleanliness, and quiet and want to use the resort as a base to explore Koh Chang · ideal for a night near the pier · may not suit people who want to walk down to the sand from their room, families who need full facilities, or anyone not comfortable getting around the island.

faq.q: Does Feel@Chill Resort have a pool, spa, and breakfast?
faq.a: There's a small outdoor pool with sun loungers for cooling off, and a café/restaurant serving Thai food and breakfast (may cost extra) · but there's no full spa or fitness center, even though some old booking-site listings mention them · it's a small resort that focuses on cleanliness and the essentials rather than a full set of facilities.
